detail: Findmypast, 18 October 2026: the 1871 and 1881 censuses and Hertfordshire Baptisms, searched for Caroline Wallis of Weston. The search that found her was a forename, a parish and a birth year with NO surname, because the 1871 index spells the family WALLACE.
Hertfordshire Baptisms, Weston: Caroline WALLIS, baptised 16 April 1862, father JOSEPH, a labourer, mother SARAH. The only Caroline Wallis baptised at Weston in the early 1860s in that set.

RG10 piece 1366, folio 41, page 14, schedule 74. JOSEPH WALLACE, head, born about 1829; SARAH, wife, born about 1831; children indexed as James (b. 1852), William (1856), Emma (1859), Eliza (1861), CAROLINE (1862, aged 9, born Weston, a straw plaiter), Joseph (1865), Jerimia (1867), Sarah (1869) and George. The index reads the surname WALLACE.

RG11 piece 1417, folio 97, page 13, schedule 81. JOSEPH WALLIS, head; SARAH, wife; EMMA, ELIZA, CAROLINE (daughter, single, 19, a straw plaiter, born Weston), JOSEPH, SARAH and GEORGE; and a lodger family, Field. The surname is Wallis here. She is single on 3 April 1881 and married at Hitchin in the last quarter of 1882.

record: What those records make of her birth
detail: Every document made when she was a girl says 1862: the baptism of April 1862, the age of nine in 1871, the age of 19 in 1881, and the 1957 death index. Her registered birth is the Caroline WALLIS of the March quarter of 1862 at Hitchin, vol 3a p230. THE 1939 REGISTER'S 'YEAR 1863', her age of 48 in the 1911 census and her 56 years 4 months in 1921 are each a year or more out. The unnamed WALLIS girl of the March quarter of 1863 (p247) is another child and not her.

It does not join this girl to Caroline Castle by a document. The join is the forename, the surname, the parish of Weston, the age and the straw plaiting; her own first child, registered as Sarah Ann Wallis in 1882, carries the forename of the household's mother. The marriage certificate of 1882 would name her father, and is the one record that would settle it.
The marriage of Joseph and Sarah Wallis, and their own baptisms; and the 1861 census, in which Caroline could not appear (the household had Eliza, born 1861, and Caroline came a year later).
